SRI.C.S.HRITHWIK -SR.PUBLIC PROSECUTOR  THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 20.06.2023, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 B.A.No.3286/23 2  ORDER
This is an application filed u/s 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure seeking pre-arrest bail.

2. The petitioner is the accused in Crime No.646 of 2022 of Medical College Police Station,
Amal Krishna P vs State Of Kerala on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195968953/
1 Kozhikode, which was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 306 IPC.
The crime was registered consequent to the suicide committed by one Bijusha, the petitioner's wife herein, by hanging.
On 16.08.2022 at 11.45, the victim was found hanging, and she died on 20.08.2022 while undergoing treatment.
The allegation against the petitioner is that, after the marriage with the victim on 18.08.2018, the petitioner used to ill-treat her mentally and physically.
It is alleged that the petitioner suspected the chastity of the victim and always created problems.
Aforesaid disputes ultimately compelled the victim to commit suicide.
As the petitioner apprehend arrest in connection with the investigation, this bail application is filed.

3. Heard Sri.A.Ranjith Narayanan, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.C.S.Hrithwik, learned Public Prosecutor for the State.
4.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is innocent of all the allegations.
Apart from the fact that there were some disputes between the petitioner and the victim, under no circumstances it can be alleged that the petitioner had committed the offence.
Adequate materials to establish the intention to pursue the victim to commit suicide are absent.
The petitioner is ready and willing to cooperate with the investigation and shall abide by any contention that may be imposed by this Court.
It is also pointed out that the 2 nd and 3rd accused mother and sister of the petitioner were already granted anticipatory bail by the Sessions Court.

The learned counsel further points out that in the report submitted by the investigating officer before the Sessions Court, while his application for bail was pending, it was mentioned that the custodial interrogation was not required,
but despite the same, the learned Sessions Court dismissed the application submitted by the petitioner.
5.
On the other hand, the learned Public Prosecutor opposes the application for bail.
The case diary was produced before this Court.

Placing reliance upon the statements of the mother, relatives and neighbours of the victim, it was pointed out that, right from the inception, there were disputes between the petitioner and the victim.
However, now the matter is under investigation and therefore, dismissal of the application is sought.
6. I have gone through the records.
As rightly pointed out by the learned Public Prosecutor, there are certain allegations of ill-treatment meted out to the victim by the petitioner herein.
The statements of the witnesses, which forms part of the case diary, would indicate the same.

All the said witnesses have stated that the petitioner was suspicious about the chastity of the victim, and the dispute arose on account of the same, which probably resulted in the victim committing suicide.
However, on a careful scrutiny of the statement, no specific instance which can be treated as the immediate reason for the death is not seen mentioned.
Even though some instances of ill-treatment were mentioned in the statements of the witnesses, the specific instance based on which the victim was persuaded to commit suicide is not very clear.
It is a matter for investigation which is now in progress.
Considering the aforesaid aspect, I am of the view that some order to protect the personal liberty of the petitioner can be passed by ensuring his cooperation with the investigation.

7. In such circumstances, this application is disposed of with the following conditions:

sentences.text: (i) The petitioner shall surrender before the Investigating officer, within a period of two weeks from today, for subjecting himself to interrogation.

(ii) After interrogation, the petitioner shall be released on bail, on the very same day of surrender upon the petitioner executing a bond for Rs 1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only) with two sureties each for the like sum, to the satisfaction of the investigating officer (iii) The petitioner shall fully cooperate with the investigation, including subjecting himself to the deemed police custody for the purpose of recovery, if any, as and when demanded.
(iv) The petitioner shall appear before the investigating officer between 10.00 a.m and 11.00 a.m every Friday until further orders.
(v) The petitioner shall also appear before the investigating officer as and when required by him.
(vi) The petitioner shall not commit any offence of similar nature while on bail.

(vii) The petitioner shall not make any attempt to contact any of the prosecution witnesses, directly or through any other person, or in any other way try to tamper with the evidence or influence any witnesses or other persons related to the investigation.
(viii) The petitioner shall not leave the State of Kerala without the permission of the trial Court.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider the application for cancellation of bail, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with the law.

Sd/-
